- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 30d mean), model frequently overshoots in next 3-5 days; apply downward correction by 2-5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to adjust; check for lagged reversal in forecast, especially days 7-14.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 30d mean, reduce by 0.1–0.3σ per day until convergence; if below, increase by 0.1–0.3σ.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts often overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to sentiment-weighted forecast adjustments.
